summary: Applies translate, rotate, scale, pivot, look-at, and post-transform alignment to SOP geometry in object/local space by changing point positions rather than COMP world transforms.

key_params.name: group
key_params.note: Restrict the transform to a point or primitive group.

key_params.name: xord
key_params.note: Overall transform order for scale, rotate, and translate.

key_params.name: vlength
key_params.note: Maintain vector attribute lengths when scaling geometry.

key_params.name: lookat
key_params.note: Orient geometry toward another object origin.

key_params.name: upvector
key_params.note: Up vector used for look-at orientation.

key_params.name: forwarddir
key_params.note: Forward axis used by look-at orientation.

key_params.name: fromx
key_params.note: Input bounds point used for X alignment.

key_params.name: tox
key_params.note: Reference bounds point used for X alignment.

key_params.name: fromy
key_params.note: Input bounds point used for Y alignment.

key_params.name: toy
key_params.note: Reference bounds point used for Y alignment.

key_params.name: fromz
key_params.note: Input bounds point used for Z alignment.

key_params.name: toz
key_params.note: Reference bounds point used for Z alignment.

common_gotchas: Transforms are baked into SOP point positions within the chain, unlike COMP-level transforms.
Different transform or rotation orders can produce different geometry from the same numeric values.
Post alignment and reference scaling need a second input when Reference Input modes are used.
Use Normals Maintain Length when scaled geometry must preserve vector attribute lengths such as normals or velocity.
key_concepts: Transform SOP edits point positions in SOP object/local space; COMP transforms move the object in world space without changing geometry coordinates.
Transform order and rotation order change the result even when translate, rotate, and scale values are identical.
Pivot, look-at, up vector, and forward direction control orientation around geometry-space axes rather than camera or component space.
Post Transform parameters align or scale geometry after the main transform, optionally using a second input as the reference bounds.
